reading_ledger.extent: Publisher’s chapter PDF freshly checked: selected pp. 19–20, 23–24, 25–29 and conclusion/reference pp. 36–38 read; p. 24 visually collated. Explicit Foucault use concerns curricular exclusion and knowledge hierarchy; p. 37 prints Knowledge/Power. This is not a whole-chapter reading or a claim to have read Foucault’s original. Freire appears on p. 20 but has no existing graph endpoint; no new biography requested. The 2016 chapter is distinct from the 1990 book and its revised 2004 edition.

Primary report’s title, six-person research-team credit, copyright 2005, selected literature-review pp. 46–48 and bibliography p. 140 entry for Walker 2002 freshly read; p. 47 visually collated. Report explicitly says Ranginui Walker cites Gramsci on domination and intellectual/moral leadership in Māori news is bad news, then explains the one-sided media discourse. Walker’s 2002 chapter, its complete evidence, and Gramsci’s original passage/edition remain unread. Tai Walker, report coauthor, is not Ranginui Walker. No whole-report reading claimed.

Freshly read selected historiographical discussion pp. 7–8 and note 48 across pp. 13–14; p. 8 and both note pages visually collated in institutional PDF. Joint authors explicitly identify Walker’s Fanon inspiration and colonial-disavowal/resistance interpretation, citing the revised 2004 book and Fanon’s 1965/1968 London editions. These originals remain unread. This is qualified named-reader evidence, not a newly verified direct quotation from Walker or an inference from shared postcolonial vocabulary.
